question.problem: Calculate the volume of the parallelepiped spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB}$, $\overset{\to }{AC}$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$, given the points $A(-1,1,1)$, $B(2,-2,1)$, $C(1,2,2)$, and $D(2,-1,4).$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the displacement vectors $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ that span the parallelepiped:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(2i-2j+k)-(-i+j+k) \\  & =3i-3j \\  & =⟨3,-3,0⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(i+2j+2k)-(-i+j+k) \\  & =2i+j+k \\  & =⟨2,1,1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AD} & =d-a \\  & =(2i-j+4k)-(-i+j+k) \\  & =3i-2j+3k \\  & =⟨3,-2,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the volume of the parallelepiped, we need to take the absolute value of the triple product of the above vectors.

Computing the triple product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot (\overset{\to }{AC}\times \overset{\to }{AD}) & =|\begin{aligned}3 & -3 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}|-(-3)\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}|+0\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =3(1\cdot 3-(-2)\cdot 1)+3(2\cdot 3-3\cdot 1)+0 \\  & =15+9 \\  & =24.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume of the corresponding parallelpiped spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ is

$$
V=|24|=24.
$$
